name: Ignorance (ajñāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 5.15–16: ignorance covers knowledge, and by it creatures are deluded; when it is destroyed by knowledge of the self, knowledge illumines the highest like the sun. 4.42: doubt is born of ignorance. 4.40: the ignorant perishes.

name: Lack of faith (aśraddhā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4.40: the faithless (aśraddadhāna), with the ignorant and the doubter, perishes; by contrast the one with faith obtains knowledge (4.39).

name: Attachment to the fruits of action (phala-saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4–6: the Lord has no longing for the fruit of action (4.14); abandoning attachment to the fruit, one does nothing though acting (4.20); the unyoked one, attached to the fruit, is bound (5.12); the renunciant and yogin acts without depending on the fruit (6.1).

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Many free of passion, fear and anger reached the Lord's state (4.10); the meditating yogin is without fear (6.14); the sage free of desire, fear and anger is forever free (5.28).

name: The pairs of opposites (dvandva)
description: The pairs such as cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour (6.7); one who has gone beyond them is not bound though acting (4.22); one free of them is easily released from bondage (5.3).

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 5.3: the constant renunciant is the one who neither hates (dveṣṭi) nor desires.

name: Excess or deficiency in eating and sleeping
description: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one given to too much sleep, nor for one who keeps awake (6.16).

name: Stain, impurity, fault (kalmaṣa, kilbiṣa, pāpa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4–6: impurities are destroyed by sacrifice (4.30); the worst sinner crosses all wrong by the raft of knowledge (4.36); stains are shaken off by knowledge (5.17) and destroyed in the seers who attain brahma-nirvāṇa (5.25); the one acting with actions placed in Brahman is not stained by sin (5.10); one doing merely bodily action incurs no fault (4.21); the calm yogin is stainless (6.27–28); the striving yogin is cleansed of faults over many births (6.45).

name: Desire (kāma)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4–6: undertakings free of desire mark the learned (4.19); the unyoked is bound, attached to the fruit through the drive of desire (5.12); the surge of desire and anger is to be withstood before leaving the body (5.23); the liberated sage is free of desire (icchā), fear and anger (5.28); the yoked one is free of craving for all desires (6.18); desires born of intention are to be abandoned without remainder (6.24).

name: Anger (krodha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4–6: those free of passion, fear and anger came to the Lord's being (4.10); the surge of desire and anger is to be withstood (5.23); ascetics free of desire and anger have brahma-nirvāṇa all around them (5.26); the sage from whom desire, fear and anger have gone is ever liberated (5.28).

name: Envy (matsara)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4.22: the one free of envy (vimatsara), content with what comes unsought and beyond the opposites, is not bound though acting.

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Knowledge taught by the truth-seers frees one from falling into delusion again (4.35); creatures are deluded because knowledge is covered by ignorance (5.15); the knower of Brahman is undeluded (5.20).

name: Passion (rāga)
description: Many free of passion, fear and anger, absorbed in the Lord, reached his state (4.10); the constant renouncer does not crave (5.3).

name: The restless mind
description: Arjuna does not see how the yoga of sameness can stand steady because of restlessness (6.33): the mind is restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, as hard to restrain as the wind (6.34); Kṛṣṇa agrees it is hard to restrain (6.35); it wanders off (6.26).

name: Doubt (saṃśaya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4.40–42: the one of doubting mind (saṃśayātman) perishes and has neither this world nor the next nor happiness; doubt is born of ignorance and lodged in the heart; the seers who attain brahma-nirvāṇa have their doubts cut (5.25); Arjuna asks the Lord to cut his doubt about the fallen yogin (6.39).

name: Enjoyments born of contact (saṃsparśaja bhoga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 5.21–22: enjoyments born of contact are wombs of suffering and have a beginning and an end; the wise do not delight in them; the one unattached to external contacts finds happiness in the self.

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 4–6: for the one whose attachment is gone action dissolves (4.23); one acting with actions placed in Brahman and abandoning attachment is unstained (5.10); yogins act abandoning attachment (5.11); one unattached to external contacts finds happiness in the self (5.21); one unattached to sense objects and actions has ascended to yoga (6.4).

name: Intention (saṅkalpa) as bondage
description: Intention is absent from the undertakings of the wise (4.19); no one becomes a yogin without renouncing it (6.2); the one ascended to yoga has renounced all intentions (6.4); desires are born of intention (6.24).

name: The sense of 'I am the doer'
description: The yoked knower of reality thinks 'I do nothing at all', holding that the senses move among their objects (5.8–9); the lord creates neither agency nor actions nor their link with fruit — svabhāva acts (5.14). Chs. 4–6 do not use the compound kartṛtva-abhimāna.
